facts.statement: The genus Stenosteus was first described by Dean in 1901.
Fossils of Stenosteus have been found in the Upper Famennian Cleveland Shale of Ohio.
facts.quote: known from the Upper Famennian Cleveland Shale of Ohio

facts.statement: The estimated skull length of Stenosteus ranges from 6 to 9 centimeters.
facts.quote: Estimated skull lengths range from 6 to 9 centimeters

facts.statement: Most known fossils of Stenosteus consist of scraps of armor and portions of tooth plates.
facts.quote: Most fossils of Stenosteus have been scraps of armor and portions of tooth-plates

facts.statement: Stenosteus is an extinct genus of medium-sized selenosteid arthrodire placoderms.
facts.quote: Stenosteus is an extinct monospecific genus of medium-sized selenosteid arthrodire placoderms

facts.statement: Stenosteus belongs to the family Selenosteidae within the clade Aspinothoracidi.
facts.quote: Stenosteus is a member of the family Selenosteidae of the clade Aspinothoracidi

facts.statement: Stenosteus lived during the Famennian stage, between 372.15 and 358.86 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Famennian to Famennian (372.15 to 358.86 million years ago)
